svg.title: Cassandra node internals - Group 4
svg.text: Inside one Cassandra 5.0.8 node (all three nodes are identical: there is no special master node)
Every node plays two roles per request: coordinator (if the driver picked it) and local replica (if it owns the token range; with RF = N = 3, every node owns every row).
Node cass1 (172.28.0.11) - same software on cass2, cass3
parses statement, reads its consistency level, picks request path
write: send to all live replicas,
reply after W acks (2 s timeout)
reply after R answers (5 s timeout)
Local replica role: storage engine (LSM tree)
Data, Partition index, Bloom filter, statistics; each cell carries a write timestamp
deletes are tombstones (kept gc_grace_seconds = 10 days by default)
compaction merges SSTables, keeps newest cell, later purges expired tombstones
Bloom filter skips SSTables that cannot hold the key (seen in our Paxos trace)
cells merged by timestamp: last write wins per cell
returns full data or an MD5 digest, as the coordinator asked
Paxos state (system.paxos table, only for LWT)
per partition: promised ballot, accepted proposal, most recent commit
written through the same commit log + memtable path
with a random live peer; seeds aid bootstrap
convict at phi > 8 -> peer marked DOWN
local opinion, not a cluster vote
coordinator keeps a write for a DOWN replica
replays it when gossip says UP
on digest mismatch at QUORUM/ALL: resolve
by timestamp, push newest cells to stale
Merkle tree per token range per replica
compare trees, stream only differing ranges
commit; quorum of the partition's replicas
plain reads and writes never use Paxos
mutation / read / digest / Paxos messages to the other replicas
V: exercised and observed in our runs
D: documented, not measured by us
